ei.title: Disliking a Food Category Versus the Food
ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: If you told me that you don't like sharp cheeses, I would believe you. If you said that you don't like the texture of very soft cheeses, I would pity you, but I would believe you. But if you say that you don't like any cheese, I don't believe you because cheeses simply don't taste, look, or feel the same. What my friend dislikes is something being called "cheese." I'm sure that he had a bad cheese experience in childhood. He ate something he didn't like and learned that "cheese" is bad. With that negative attitude, he quickly rejected anything else called "cheese" (and very likely did not have a wide experience with cheeses anyway), reinforcing his belief that "cheese" is bad. As a result, this friend, who is in other respects normal, cannot bear to eat anything that he believes is called "cheese." He actually thinks that there is some flavor or property of cheese that makes it taste bad to him. But that is not the case: cheeses don't share a particular texture or flavor or source. He hates the category, not the actual stuff.

questions.passage: As a result, this friend, who is in other respects normal, cannot bear to eat anything that he __________ (believe) is called "cheese."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: believe → believes (3인칭 단수 현재, 주어 he에 수일치)
det.analysis: 주어 he에 3인칭 단수 현재 수일치가 필요하므로 believe → believes. 'anything that he believes is called cheese'에서 he believes는 삽입절

questions.passage: If you told me that you don't like sharp cheeses, I would believe you. If you said that you don't like the texture of very soft cheeses, I would pity you, but I would believe you. But if you say that you don't like any cheese, I don't believe you because cheeses simply don't taste, look, or feel the same. What my friend dislikes is something being called "cheese." I'm sure that he had __________ in childhood. He ate something he didn't like and learned that "cheese" is bad. With that negative attitude, he quickly rejected anything else called "cheese" (and very likely did not have a wide experience with cheeses anyway), reinforcing his belief that "cheese" is bad. As a result, this friend, who is in other respects normal, cannot bear to eat anything that he believes is called "cheese." He actually thinks that there is some flavor or property of cheese that makes it taste bad to him. But that is not the case: cheeses don't share a particular texture or flavor or source. He hates the category, not the actual stuff.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나는 그가 어린 시절에 ______을(를) 했다고 확신한다
det.analysis: 어린 시절의 ______이 치즈 혐오의 원인이다. a wide experience(폭넓은 경험)은 반대로 경험이 부족했다는 맥락. a particular texture(특정 질감)과 some flavor(어떤 맛)은 뒤에 나오는 내용. a bad cheese experience(나쁜 치즈 경험)가 정답 ←정답
det.tip: a bad cheese experience=나쁜 치즈 경험

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis: 마지막 부분에서 친구가 치즈의 어떤 속성이 나쁜 맛을 낸다고 생각하지만 '사실은 그렇지 않다: 치즈들은 ______.' don't taste the same(같은 맛이 아니다)은 앞에 나온 표현. cannot bear(견딜 수 없다)는 친구 행동. bad experience(나쁜 경험)는 어린 시절 이야기. don't share a particular texture or flavor or source(특정 질감/맛/출처를 공유하지 않는다)가 정답 ←정답
det.tip: 치즈는 공통된 특정 질감, 맛, 출처가 없다는 핵심 주장
